The fleet file has the desktop as **desk-01**. Since you only want the free space on D:, a script is enough. It answers directly and doesn't start a Claude session on the desktop, so it uses no usage. Run this from your lap-01 WSL shell:

```zsh
/mnt/c/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe desk-wsl 'df -h /mnt/d'
```

- It uses the Windows `ssh.exe` because your WSL distro has no SSH key.
- It connects to the desktop's WSL lane on port 2222, where Windows' D: drive appears as `/mnt/d`.
- The `Avail` column is the free space.

If you'd rather have the desktop's Claude answer, run this instead. It starts a Claude session on the desktop, which costs usage, and you may get a permission prompt:

```zsh
/mnt/c/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe desk-wsl 'hostname && claude -p "Report the free space on the D drive (/mnt/d) in GB. Run df -h /mnt/d and reply with just the hostname and the Avail value." < /dev/null'
```

`hostname` shows which machine answered.

**One thing to check:** the fleet file I found was made for desk-01, not your laptop, so I took the `desk-wsl` alias from it. If the laptop's `~/.ssh/config` doesn't define `desk-wsl`, ssh will say it can't resolve the hostname. In that case, use whatever alias the laptop has for the desktop's WSL lane on port 2222.

Run this from your WSL shell on lap-01:

```zsh
/mnt/c/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe desk-win '(Get-PSDrive D).Free / 1GB'
```

It prints the free space on desk-01's D: drive in GB, for example `412.73`. If you'd rather see used and free space in bytes, swap the quoted part for `Get-PSDrive D | Select-Object Used,Free`.

**Why this command:**
- **No Claude needed.** Checking free space is a one-line script, so it runs PowerShell directly over SSH instead of starting a Claude session on the desktop. That's faster and doesn't use any Claude usage.
- **`desk-win` (port 22)** is the desktop's Windows SSH entry, which is meant for PowerShell commands like this one. It logs in as `ssh-admin`, which can read drive info.
- **The Windows `ssh.exe`** is needed because WSL has no SSH key of its own; the Windows SSH client does.

**Two caveats:**
- The fleet file I read was generated for desk-01, not lap-01. So I'm assuming your laptop's Windows SSH config also has a `desk-win` alias. If you get "Could not resolve hostname", that alias is missing on the laptop.
- The fleet notes list this kind of command over port 22 as untested. If it fails, use the desktop's WSL entry instead (same idea, tested route):
  ```zsh
  /mnt/c/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe desk-wsl 'df -h /mnt/d'
  ```
  This works only if D: is mounted at `/mnt/d` in the desktop's WSL.

Run this from your lap-01 WSL shell:

```zsh
/mnt/c/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe desk-win 'hostname; "{0:N2} GB free of {1:N2} GB" -f ((Get-PSDrive D).Free/1GB), (((Get-PSDrive D).Used + (Get-PSDrive D).Free)/1GB)'
```

**How it works:**
- **No Claude session.** Checking free space only needs a short script, so this doesn't start a Claude session on the desktop. That saves usage and avoids a permission prompt on that side.
- **How it connects.** It uses the Windows `ssh.exe` because WSL holds no SSH key. It connects to `desk-win`, which is the desktop's Windows shell on port 22. That account (`ssh-admin`) runs PowerShell, so the remote part is written as PowerShell.
- **Output.** `hostname` prints first, which tells you the desktop answered. Then you get a line like `123.45 GB free of 931.51 GB`.

**Things to check:**
- **Untested route.** Running a script over port 22 hasn't been tested in this fleet yet. If it fails, use the desktop's WSL shell and read the drive from there:
  ```zsh
  /mnt/c/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe desk-wsl 'hostname && df -h /mnt/d'
  ```
- **Fleet file mismatch.** The fleet file in this session says "Rendered for desk-01", not lap-01. I took `desk-win` and `desk-wsl` from its desktop section, but I haven't checked that your laptop's `~/.ssh/config` defines them. If ssh says it can't resolve the host, look there first.
